positions.commentary: The speaker suggests that Costco possesses hidden pricing power and fits the criteria of a high-quality business with a long growth runway and smart capital allocation.
The speaker identifies buying PayPal at 50 times earnings as one of their biggest mistakes because they overpaid on a business that turned out not to be good.
The speaker states that the investment philosophy of Baskin is to invest in high quality businesses and that they look for the best companies with the best management teams.
The speaker lists Mastercard as one of the few highest quality businesses in the world that investors can name.
The speaker references past concerns about T-Mobile disrupting Amazon but concludes that investors should trust the management team and be very lazy with their portfolio.
The speaker praises Adobe's management team, their pace of work, integration of AI into workflows, and believes they will maintain pricing power despite subscription risks.
The speaker expresses excitement about the future of big tech companies over the next 10 to 15 years.

thesis: The episode argues that investors should focus on high-quality businesses with exceptional management teams and long growth runways, even if current valuations appear high. The speakers emphasize the importance of being 'lazy' with portfolios by trusting management, while acknowledging specific past mistakes like selling Meta too early or overpaying for PayPal.
